# docs/ — what belongs here

The rules for the tree as a whole: which area a statement belongs in, and where
new material goes. `docs/index.md` is the reader's entry point; this file is the
agent's — they are not copies of each other.

## Belongs here

- The area table below, and nothing about any one area's content.
- The "where new material goes" routing rule.

## Does not belong here

| Instead of | Put it in |
| -- | -- |
| A statement about one area's admission rules | that area's own `_structure.md` |
| Page content | the area itself |

## Areas

Declared in `_areas.yml`, in nav order. These are the areas kiln seeds:

| Area | Holds |
| -- | -- |
| `architecture/` | How the repo is put together now. |
| `guides/` | How to use what the repo builds, and how to develop it. |
| `runbooks/` | Procedures with judgement calls or gates. Optional. |
| `reference/` | Generated reference, such as the API. |
| `releases/` | What each release carries, and the status of its scope. |
| `specs/` | Work: epics, features, stories, their design and open questions. |
| `adr/` | Choices between real alternatives. |

- A repo may add an area: declare it in `_areas.yml` and give it its own
  `_structure.md` and `index.md`. Its rules live there, so this file needs no
  edit for it.
- Every area's rules live in its own `_structure.md`; this file only lists them.
- `_*.md` files never ship in the built site (`exclude_docs: "_*"`), and no page
  links to one.
- `mkdocs.yml`'s `nav:` is a derived region, written by `task docs:generate`
  from `docs/_areas.yml`, the tree and each page's title — do not hand-edit
  it.

## Where new material goes

- Behaviour as it is now → `architecture/`, or `guides/` if it is about using or
  developing the repo. Never duplicated into a spec.
- A choice between real alternatives → a new ADR under `adr/`; a change to one →
  that ADR, revised in place.
- Work to do, or a record of work done → an epic under `specs/epics/`.
- An idea not yet agreed as work → a row in `specs/ideas/index.md`, and a page
  beside it when the row is not enough.
- What ships when → `releases/`.
- An operational procedure → `runbooks/`.
- An open question → the epic or feature it blocks, until it becomes an ADR or a
  rejected option recorded there.
- History, evidence, what a review changed → the commit message.

These docs describe only this repository. A requirement that came from another
repository is written here in full, as this repository's own;
`specs/_structure.md` says how a dependency on another repository is written.

## Package docs

Each package under `packages/` ships its own docs site, included in the root
site as an entry under `Packages` (derived from `packages`; an `include` area in
`_areas.yml` retitles or moves it). The root `docs/` holds only cross-package
material.

A package's `docs/` has this shape:

- `index.md`, the package's entry page.
- `guides/`, with kebab-case pages.
- `reference/`, generated from the package's doc comments; it is not
  naming-checked.
- `changelog.md`, which holds only a snippet include of the package's
  `CHANGELOG.md`.
- No `adr/`, `specs/`, `releases/`, `plans/` or `runbooks/`: those are
  cross-package, and live in the root `docs/`.

Beside `docs/`, a package carries:

- `CHANGELOG.md`, in Keep a Changelog form, with an `## [Unreleased]` heading.
- `[project.urls]` in its `pyproject.toml`: `Documentation`, `Source`,
  `Changelog` and `Issues`.
- A `README.md` whose links are all absolute, because PyPI and GitHub render it
  outside the site.

A package page links only within its own `docs/`; a link that resolves outside
it fails the package's standalone strict build.

## Checks

`kiln doctor`'s `docs-structure` check enforces kiln's docs policy: every
non-optional area in `docs/_areas.yml` exists and has both a `_structure.md` and
an `index.md`; ADRs are named `ADR-<nnnn>.md`, numbered without gaps, and carry
a valid `**Status:**` line; every relative link resolves, including anchors; no
shipped page links to a `_*.md` file; there is no `specs/ideas.md`, and every
page under `specs/ideas/` is kebab-case and linked from its `index.md`; and one
instruction file links this file and `docs/index.md` (`AGENTS.md`, through
kiln's block), while any other links that file or imports it with an
`@AGENTS.md` line.

`kiln doctor`'s `docs-generate` check confirms that the derived regions — the
nav, the spec board, the epic list and each release's Scope table — are current,
and that every epic, feature and release page's metadata table follows
`specs/_structure.md` and that no epic's or feature's state contradicts its
work.

## Keeping it honest

Check for these when changing the tree, and report what you find rather than
fixing it silently — some of it is deliberate:

- A derived region edited by hand: `task lint` fails, and `task docs:generate`
  overwrites it.
- An epic's state contradicts its features, or a feature's its stories.
- Two ADRs decide the same topic, or an ADR's Decision changed
  (`git log --follow docs/adr/ADR-<nnnn>.md`) with no Background entry saying
  so.
- Design prose collecting in a top-level page instead of under its feature.
- A `progress.md`, `decisions.md` or `overview.md` has appeared; each restates
  what the epics, ADRs or README already own.
- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` describing the tree instead of linking
  to it. `README.md` is for people and links to the specs board and the ADR
  log, saying what each is for. `AGENTS.md` is for agents: it carries kiln's
  block and links to `README.md` for context. `CLAUDE.md` imports `AGENTS.md`
  with `@AGENTS.md` and holds only what is Claude-only.
- Agent directives in `README.md`, or developer setup prose in `AGENTS.md`.
- A `README.md` inside `docs/`: MkDocs drops one that sits beside an `index.md`,
  and the strict build fails.
